q: Which nerve supplies sensation to the larynx above the cords?
why: The RLN supplies sensation below the cords.

q: Which intrinsic laryngeal muscle is the only abductor of the vocal cords?
why: All intrinsic muscles are supplied by the RLN except cricothyroid (superior laryngeal nerve).
Inspiratory suggests laryngeal; expiratory suggests tracheobronchial.

q: Which feature favours epiglottitis over croup?
o: Drooling, leaning forward and absence of cough
why: Rapid deterioration, muffled voice and odynophagia.

q: What is the usual cause of croup?
why: Treat with oral dexamethasone, nebulised budesonide or adrenaline.

Which is a relative contraindication to AFOI?
o: Uncooperative patient or local anaesthetic allergy

q: How is the cricothyroid (transtracheal) injection performed?
o: 22G needle through the cricothyroid membrane, aspirate air, inject and withdraw quickly
why: Patient coughs, spreading LA below the cords.
